# T-MED Social Media Audit & Short-Form Marketing Skill

## Purpose
Protect AMilliMATRiX and CARBON° reputation while improving attention, qualified engagement, and commercially useful outcomes. This is an operational checklist/playbook, not model training.

## Required preflight
1. Read the current T-MED mandate, relevant owner directives, current channel/account identity, and the existing authorized publication/review boundary. Newer valid authority supersedes stale prompt text.
2. Identify the exact public asset/post and source asset. Record platform, URL/ID, publish time, caption, cover, video/audio, CTA, claimed owner/brand, evidence source and current status.
3. Prefer direct authenticated public-surface readback. Analytics captions, filenames, thumbnails, or prior reports alone do not prove what appears in the whole video.
4. If the platform or visual asset cannot be inspected, label frame/audio/brand audit UNKNOWN. Do not report PASS; do not guess from filenames, captions, or a thumbnail. Record the exact access blocker and next lawful route.
5. Distinguish observed fact, owner-supplied claim, model inference, and unknown. Never convert an unverified claim into public proof.

## Brand-safety and visual integrity gate — critical
Review the entire creative, not just its text:
- Every frame, cover, overlay, screen recording, browser tab, URL, watermark, logo, business name, contact detail, QR code, audio track, subtitle and end card.
- Check that the depicted business/product/site is the intended AMilliMATRiX/CARBON° subject or is clearly and legitimately contextualized. Flag unintended third-party businesses, unrelated client sites, external logos, wrong company names, exposed credentials/private data, stale mock-ups, unrelated stock footage, and misleading interface screenshots.
- Confirm that captions, visuals and CTA tell the same story. Avoid a brand-owned account appearing to advertise or claim someone else's business.
- Verify source ownership/permission and music/voice/visual usage rights for the specific asset/plan. Do not presume public availability equals commercial permission.
- Check claims against the current canonical evidence and scope. No fabricated milestones, performance, customer results, certifications, guarantees or delivery claims.
- If a critical mismatch is found, stop further reuse/publication of that asset, preserve the evidence, and route an exact correction item to its existing authorized owner. Do not silently delete, edit or repost live material unless a current explicit authorization covers that action. A proposed removal is not a completed takedown; confirm platform state after any authorized correction.

## Short-form creative standard
Default deliverable for TikTok, YouTube Shorts and similar feeds: one strong, self-contained vertical cut of 15–30 seconds unless the brief or a verified platform constraint calls for another length.
- First 0–2 seconds: a concrete curiosity, customer problem, counterintuitive truth, visible result, or human moment. No generic logo intro, abstract hype or “we are building” preamble.
- One audience, one problem/desire, one main idea, one proof point and one next action per post.
- Show proof with the strongest relevant real asset/demo. Use readable on-screen copy, purposeful pacing, clean audio, legible captions, and a clear ending/CTA. Keep faces, logos, device screens and key text inside platform-safe areas.
- Start from the viewer's intent and context. Use curiosity without bait-and-switch; empathy without presuming a defect; specificity without overwhelming jargon; proof without overclaiming.
- Sales psychology: be courteous and relevant; listen before pitching; ask, do not assume; state why something may be useful without shaming or implying unauthorized access; respond to the audience's actual need. No pressure, deception or false urgency.
- Brand identity is consistent but restrained. Do not spend the opening seconds on repeated logo animations or generic slogans.
- Derive platform versions from a clean master, not from a visibly watermarked or low-quality export. Check audio and license status before use.
- Produce a useful cutdown and caption rather than stretching a concept to fill a longer timeline. A 30-second target is not a demand to cut away needed context; if longer is justified, state why.

## Performance review and learning loop
For every published asset, read back the available metrics after a meaningful observation window:
- publish date/time, video duration, views/reach, likes, comments, shares, average watch time/completion rate, follows or clicks/conversions when actually available;
- compute engagement rate from a defined denominator and compare posts only when the metric definitions and observation windows match;
- identify hook, topic, visual approach, length, proof, CTA and audience intent; separate correlation from demonstrated cause;
- compare repeated concepts for meaningful creative variation. Do not repost the same idea with only cosmetic caption changes unless the test question is explicit;
- select next content based on evidence: retain what earns qualified attention, change a weak hook/visual/length/CTA, and retire material that is inaccurate, off-brand or rights-unclear.
No fabricated analytics. Missing watch-time or conversion fields remain UNKNOWN, not zero.

## Review priority
1. Critical: unintended third-party business/brand, private or credential leakage, false claim, rights issue, wrong external link/contact, materially misleading visual.
2. High: wrong audience or product, unreadable/watermarked creative, unverified proof, unapproved CTA, repeated off-brand content.
3. Medium: weak hook, long setup, generic captions, repetitive content, poor audio/pacing.
4. Low: cosmetic polish that does not materially affect clarity or trust.

## Output contract
Return a short prioritized table with: post URL/ID, date, issue, evidence seen, severity/confidence, recommended correction, current action authority, owner and readback needed. Separate confirmed visual findings from metadata-only signals. Never state “audited clean” unless the actual asset was inspected end-to-end.

## Publication and correction controls
- Existing ownership and authority boundaries remain in force. This skill does not grant new publication, deletion, schedule, account, or customer-contact authority.
- Do not create duplicate trackers, campaigns, queues, workers or approval paths. Use the existing T-MED / ROOT / Intake records.
- A prepared draft is not a published post. A publish request is not a published result. A deletion request is not a confirmed removal.
- Verify changed posts from the platform after any authorized write; preserve pre-change URL, copy, evidence and a change receipt.

## Acceptance
Pass only after the specific video/post was opened and visually/audio inspected, all critical brand and evidence gates passed (or exact corrections were made with authority and platform readback), and the review receipt was persisted and independently read back. Any uninspected creative is NOT VERIFIED.


## Research references and operating implications (reviewed 2026-10-25)

1. **TikTok for Business — Creative advertising guide:** https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/guides/what-is-ad-creative-guide
   - Native-feeling, short, authentic and testable creative; hook viewers quickly; tell a relevant story; use captions; deliver value or emotion early; test distinct variants and improve using engagement, watch time and conversion evidence.
2. **YouTube Help — Shorts search & discovery:** https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/11914225
   - Recommendations depend on viewer personalization and actual response: whether people choose to watch or ignore, whether they stay, average view duration / average percentage viewed, and enjoyment signals. YouTube states there is no minimum publishing cadence required for good performance. Do not equate more posts with guaranteed reach.
3. **YouTube Blog — Shorts deep dive:** https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-shorts-deep-dive/
   - Start with an immediate hook, use a distinct authentic story, build curiosity then satisfy it; judge thumbnails and title in context of the feed, and make creative variation deliberate.
4. **Scott Edinger, Harvard Business Review — Sales Reps, Stop Asking Leading Questions (2017):** https://hbr.org/2017/03/sales-reps-stop-asking-leading-questions
   - Consultative selling fails when it feels like a checklist/interrogation. Use genuine give-and-take, let the buyer describe priorities, reflect what was heard, and then assess fit. Do not presume a prospect's problem or lead with an unsolicited “fix”.

These are starting references, not a guarantee of virality. Apply them with the brand-safety gate and measure per-post results. When data fields such as average view duration or completion are unavailable, do not invent them; obtain a platform-native readback or retain UNKNOWN.


## Reference-account patterns to test (researched 2026-10-25; not for copying)

1. **Semrush B2B TikTok pattern (secondary analytics review):** Socialinsider's first-half 2026 analysis reports 92 videos, 81.8K total engagements and 1.37% average engagement rate. It notes that many top posts reuse a recognizable format: an internal social lead reacting to relatable marketing-work moments. Source: https://www.socialinsider.io/blog/tiktok-for-b2b/
   - Adaptation hypothesis for AMX: a recognizable recurring host/voice explaining a real builder, sales or workflow problem in plain language; make the human/customer situation the story and the software the proof. Test against formal engineering-status updates.
   - The published statistics are third-party-reported and are not independently verified by this skill.

2. **South African niche-retail pattern:** 4Time's agency case study of SA Baking Supplies reports 14,000 followers, 43,000 likes, 1,484 comments, 4,383 shares and 77 videos exceeding 10K views. The case attributes results to niche relevance and repeatable short-form storytelling. Source: https://www.4time.co.za/from-zero-to-2-5-million-views-how-short-form-video-transformed-a-baking-brands-digital-presence/
   - Adaptation hypothesis: stay recognizably focused on AMX's audience (small business owners, operators and builders), build repeatable series, and use concrete real-world examples rather than broad “future of AI” announcements.
   - Metrics and causal explanations are agency-reported; use them as a directional reference, not audited benchmark data.

3. **TikTok Business / SnapWireless product-demo pattern:** TikTok's published case study reports a six-day campaign with 130 conversions, conversion rate above 1.6% and 8x return on ad spend. Its description emphasizes short, sharp product demonstration creative plus an explicit sales action. Source: https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/inspiration/snapwireless
   - Adaptation hypothesis: every offer-led clip should show the use case quickly, provide one credible proof point, and use one measurable next step. This is a paid-campaign case; do not conflate it with organic performance.

4. **Platform ranking reality:** YouTube says Shorts distribution uses viewer choice (watch vs ignore), whether viewers stay, average view duration / average percentage viewed, and enjoyment signals; it does not require a minimum posting cadence. Source: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/11914225
   - Operational implication: consistency helps build a testable content system, but volume alone is not the goal. Improve the hook and watch-through first, and measure downstream qualified action when available.

### AMX experiment design
Use three distinct, repeatable creative lanes rather than one generic corporate format:
- **Show, don't announce:** visible demo/proof, what changes for the customer, and a clean end result.
- **Human problem / insight:** an understandable scenario, mistake, misconception or buyer concern, explained respectfully; no invented customer story.
- **Unexpected but on-brand hook:** humour, contrast, or curiosity that is resolved by the actual product/evidence within the clip.

For each trial, state one hypothesis, use a distinct hook/creative, preserve the actual asset and publish metadata, and compare post-level results after a consistent observation window. Keep organic and paid results separate. Retain winners as formats, not as scripts to duplicate verbatim. Never claim virality or buyer conversion without evidence.
